title: White Sox’s Braden Montgomery becomes fifth player to hit walk-off home run in MLB debut
content:
With one swing of the bat, Chicago White Sox rookie Braden Montgomery did something only four other players in the history of Major League Baseball had ever done before: hit a walk-off home run in their big-league debut.

In hitting a walk-off two-run homer in the 10th inning to give Chicago a 6-5 win over the Atlanta Braves on Tuesday night, Montgomery joined the following players, per MLB.com’s Sarah Langs:

The homer completed a 2-for-5 and three-RBI debut for the 23-year-old right fielder, and it came against Raisel Iglesias, whose 0.87 ERA entering Tuesday ranked fifth among all relievers.

Ranked as the White Sox No. 1 prospect by The Athletic’s Keith Law, Montgomery was called up Tuesday after a strong showing between Double and Triple A. Over 56 games (27 at Double A, 29 at Triple A), Montgomery posted a .970 OPS with 10 homers and 41 RBIs.

“He understands the strike zone and doesn’t chase much from either side of the plate, but swings hard all the time, especially left-handed, trading off some swing and miss for more damage on contact,” Law wrote.

Acquired as part of the 2024 deal that sent left-hander Garrett Crochet to the Boston Red Sox, Montgomery is the final prospect of Chicago’s return to make his big-league debut. The trade netted the White Sox catcher Kyle Teel, right-hander Wikelman Gonzalez and infielder Chase Meidroth, in addition to Montgomery. Montgomery was Boston’s first-round pick out of Texas A&M.

With a 35-31 record, the White Sox are just a half-game behind the Cleveland Guardians for the American League Central lead. If the season ended Tuesday, Chicago would have the second AL wild-card spot.
